label: copied-back "a" fed in early in the copy phase
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the input token is the letter a (the model feeding back its own copied a). That means the original sequence had a at position 0 or 1. It is restricted to the first few copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, rarely 3) and to absolute step t <= 9, so it is strongest in short sequences (L 3-6). Magnitude is highest at recall_idx 1, where the input is orig(0) = a right after <DEL> (85% of mass; top activations ~4.3 are all a x y z <DEL> [a]). A fed-back a at recall_idx 2 gives weaker activations. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, never on an a seen for the first time, never on any other token, and almost never on a fed-back a later in the copy phase or in long sequences (L 8-9).

issues: The core claims hold up. Every activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000), every one is on in_tok == a (share 1.000), and none occur in the original or delimiter phases. recall_idx 1 holds 85.1% of the mass, recall_idx 2 holds 14.7% and recall_idx 3 holds 0.2%. Max activation is 4.30. The reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.807, R 0.966, F1 0.879.

The t <= 9 cutoff leaves a systematic class of false positives. On the test split, precision of fed-back a broken out by (recall_idx, L) is: r=1 for L=3..7 is about 1.0, r=1 L=8 (t=9) is 0.59, r=1 L=9 is 0.11. For r=2: L=4 and L=5 are about 0.99, L=6 (t=8) is 0.67, L=7 (t=9) is 0.05, L=3 (the last step, to_go=0) is 0.65. So r=2 at L=7, t=9 (about 2,700 predicted steps, about 95% inactive) is the largest false-positive class. The predicate includes it on purpose.

The explanation gets its own false positives wrong. It says the remaining false positives are 'recall_idx 2 in sequences of length 7-8, at step 8-9'. With recall_idx=2 and t<=9, L can be at most 7, so L=8 cannot occur. It also leaves out the substantial false-positive class at recall_idx 1, L=8, t=9: 41% of those steps are inactive, about 1,100 steps. Test misses show it directly, e.g. 'a k g x o f g p <DEL> *a*' is inactive.

The real boundary depends on recall_idx and L, not on a single t cutoff. recall_idx 1 stays reliable up to L=7 and is partial at L=8. recall_idx 2 is reliable only for L=4-5 and partial at L=6. Even the simple (recall_idx<=2) & (t<=8) beats the stated predicate on test: F1 0.911 vs 0.879.

The label itself ('copied-back a fed in early in the copy phase') is broadly fair, but the predicate's bounds are wrong. The leftover false positives inside the refined predicate (r=1 L=8, r=2 L=6) did not show an obvious token or history pattern in the misses output.
skeptic.revised_label: copied-back "a" at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, L<=8) or the second copy step in short sequences (recall_idx 2, L<=6)

final_label: copied-back "a" at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, L<=8) or the second copy step in short sequences (recall_idx 2, L<=6)
